source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MCPE-112543:Redstone lamps don't show up on maps
source_meta._title: Redstone lamps do not show on maps

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.12.2 in a single-player world. Use Creative mode with cheats enabled so the supplied /fill command can be executed and an Empty Map can be obtained without adding unrelated crafting steps. A new Superflat world is a practical deterministic choice because it provides a level surface with a visually consistent block layer beneath the lamps.
preconditions: Launch the exact recommended affected version, Minecraft Java Edition 1.12.2, rather than the listed fix version 24w35a.
Use a world in which the player has permission to execute commands. For single-player, create or open the world with cheats enabled.
Use Creative mode as a practical execution choice; the report does not require a specific game mode.
Stand on an open, level, solid surface with at least a 10-by-10-block area of air beside the player so the 9-by-9 lamp platform will not replace existing structures.

Keep the blocks directly beneath the future lamp platform intact. The supplied command places lamps at the player's current Y level, from one to nine blocks away in both the positive X and positive Z directions.
Do not add levers, redstone blocks, or other power sources; the supplied command creates ordinary unpowered redstone lamps.
Use an unmodified world without datapacks or mods that change maps, redstone lamps, or block map colors.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft launcher with the Minecraft Java Edition 1.12.2 installation selected, launch the game, and wait for the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The main menu identifies the running game as Minecraft 1.12.2.

steps.action: Create a new single-player Creative-mode world with cheats enabled. For a deterministic level work area, select the Superflat world type. Enter the world and wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded world, can fly, and has permission to use commands.

steps.action: Move to a clear section of the level surface. Stand still on a solid block and verify that there is open air in the square extending at least nine blocks in the positive X direction and nine blocks in the positive Z direction from the player's position. The exact facing direction does not affect the relative-coordinate command.
steps.success_cue: There is enough unobstructed space beside the player for a 9-by-9 horizontal lamp platform, with the normal surface blocks remaining directly below that space.

steps.action: Open the in-game chat input using the default chat control.
steps.exact_input: T
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's command exactly as supplied, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not modernize or otherwise alter the block identifier or coordinates.
steps.exact_input: /fill ~1 ~ ~1 ~9 ~ ~9 minecraft:redstone_lamp
steps.success_cue: The command completes successfully and a horizontal 9-by-9 area of 81 unpowered redstone lamps is visible beside the player's original position.

steps.action: Wait for the lamp platform and surrounding terrain to finish rendering. If necessary, fly slightly upward to confirm the platform is complete, but remain close to it and do not place blocks over the lamps.
steps.success_cue: All 81 lamp blocks are loaded in a complete 9-by-9 square, their top faces are unobstructed, and player movement is responsive.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory control.
steps.exact_input: E
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open, with item tabs and the nine hotbar slots visible.

steps.action: Locate the item named Empty Map in the Creative inventory and place one Empty Map into any hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the inventory interface.
steps.success_cue: One Empty Map is present in a known hotbar slot.

steps.action: Close the inventory, then select the hotbar slot containing the Empty Map by pressing its corresponding number key or scrolling the mouse wheel until that slot is highlighted.
steps.exact_input: E, then the number key corresponding to the Empty Map's hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The Empty Map is shown as the held item and its hotbar slot has the active selection outline.

steps.action: Position the player on or immediately beside the 9-by-9 lamp platform so the platform is close to the location where the map will be created. Keep the platform's top surface uncovered and remain in the Overworld.
steps.success_cue: The player is within a few blocks of the lamp platform, the platform is loaded, and the Empty Map remains selected.

steps.action: Use the selected Empty Map with the default use-item control to create and begin filling the map. Keep the resulting filled map selected and remain near the lamp platform while its terrain pixels populate.
steps.exact_input: Right-click
steps.success_cue: The Empty Map has changed into a filled map, and terrain-colored pixels have populated rather than the map remaining entirely blank.

steps.action: Adjust the camera downward as needed so the held filled map is fully visible on screen. Do not switch hotbar slots, leave the area, cover the lamps, or alter the lamp platform before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse downward until the held map is clearly visible
steps.success_cue: The filled map is selected, visibly displayed in the player's hands, and has updated while the player is beside the loaded redstone-lamp platform.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just brought the updated filled map into clear view while standing on or beside the loaded, unobstructed 9-by-9 redstone-lamp platform. Begin map-content observation now without changing the selected item or world blocks.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world type, seed, coordinates, or the material beneath the lamps. Creative mode and a new Superflat world are practical choices that make the supplied command and map acquisition deterministic while retaining a solid block layer beneath the lamps.
The report does not explicitly distinguish between powered and unpowered lamps. The supplied /fill command creates unpowered redstone lamps, so no power source has been added.

The report does not prescribe crafting the map versus obtaining it from Creative inventory. Creative inventory is used to avoid unrelated crafting while still performing the required action of using an Empty Map to create a filled map.
No external verification was required; the reproduction plan preserves the report's exact command and uses the first listed affected version.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition, vanilla single-player using two launcher installations: 20w16a to create the pre-upgrade world and filled map, followed by the affected snapshot 20w17a to open the same world. Use the same game directory, or otherwise ensure that the 20w17a installation can access the world created in 20w16a. Creative mode is used only as a practical way to obtain and update a map without crafting or survival requirements.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can start both Java Edition snapshot 20w16a and snapshot 20w17a.

Snapshot 20w17a must not create the test world; the same world must first exist and contain a filled map in a version from before 20w17a. This plan uses 20w16a, the immediately preceding snapshot, as the deterministic setup version.
Do not optimize the world with "Erase cached data" and do not use the startup arguments "--forceUpgrade --eraseCache" before reproducing; the report identifies those operations as repair procedures.
Use an unmodified vanilla client with no datapacks, mods, or resource packs required by the test.
Keep a backup of the 20w16a world because opening the working copy in 20w17a upgrades that copy.
No particular world seed, coordinates, map scale, difficulty, or graphics setting is specified by the report.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation that runs Java Edition snapshot 20w16a, then start the game with that installation.
steps.exact_input: Select installation/version "20w16a" and press Play.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and displays version 20w16a.

steps.action: Open the single-player world list and begin creating a new world. Give it a recognizable name such as "MC-179858 pre-20w17a" so that the same world can be identified after changing versions.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World; world name: MC-179858 pre-20w17a
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows the chosen test-world name.

steps.action: Set the world to Creative mode to permit direct access to an Empty Map without crafting, then create the world. Leave the seed and world-generation settings at their defaults.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in the new 20w16a world and the Creative-mode hotbar is visible at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Wait before interacting until the spawn terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby surface terrain is visible, missing chunks are no longer appearing around the player, and movement responds without world-loading pauses.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory action, whose default key is E. Select the Search Items tab, enter "map" in the search field, and place the item specifically labeled "Empty Map" into any hotbar slot. The hotbar is the nine-slot row along the bottom of the screen.
steps.exact_input: E; search text: map; move one Empty Map to a hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: One Empty Map is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory and select the hotbar slot containing the Empty Map. Use the corresponding number key 1 through 9 or scroll the mouse wheel until that slot is highlighted.
steps.exact_input: E to close inventory; then the applicable hotbar key 1-9 or mouse wheel
steps.success_cue: The Empty Map's hotbar slot is highlighted and the player is holding the Empty Map.

steps.action: Use the held Empty Map once with the use-item control, whose default input is right-click. Do this while standing in the loaded Overworld terrain.
steps.exact_input: right-click once
steps.success_cue: The Empty Map has changed into a filled Map, the map is visible in the player's hands, and nearby terrain begins appearing on it.

steps.action: Keep the filled Map selected and move around within its coverage area long enough to populate a useful baseline. Walk with W, or double-tap Space to begin Creative flight and then use W. Keep the player marker within the map border and continue until the map contains multiple areas of rendered surface terrain rather than remaining mostly blank.
steps.exact_input: W; optionally Space twice to toggle Creative flight
steps.success_cue: The filled Map remains in the active hotbar slot and shows a substantial area of surface terrain created while the world is still running in 20w16a.

steps.action: Stop moving while still somewhere covered by the filled Map, then open the pause menu and save the world by returning to the title screen. Do not discard the Map; leave it in the player's inventory or active hotbar slot.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The game has returned to the title screen after saving the 20w16a world with the filled Map in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Close Minecraft completely so the world files are no longer in use.
steps.exact_input: Quit Game
steps.success_cue: The 20w16a game process has closed.

steps.action: Create a backup of the saved world before upgrading it. Copy the entire folder for "MC-179858 pre-20w17a" from the active game directory's saves folder to a separate backup location. Do not use the backup copy for the reproduction; retain it as the pre-20w17a source world.
steps.exact_input: Copy .minecraft/saves/<test-world-folder> to a separate backup location
steps.success_cue: There are two copies of the world: the working copy in the game's saves directory and a separate untouched 20w16a backup.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, switch to an installation that runs the affected Java Edition snapshot 20w17a and start the game. Ensure this installation uses the game directory containing the working copy of the test world.
steps.exact_input: Select installation/version "20w17a" and press Play.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and displays version 20w17a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, select the working world named "MC-179858 pre-20w17a", and load it in 20w17a. If Minecraft warns that the world was created in a different version or recommends making a backup, proceed with opening the working copy because a separate backup was already made. Do not choose Optimize World and do not erase cached data.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> select MC-179858 pre-20w17a -> Play Selected World; confirm the version warning if shown
steps.success_cue: The same world has opened in 20w17a at the player's saved position.

steps.action: Wait until the upgraded world is fully ready before updating the Map. Do not continue while chunks are missing or while player movement is unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: Surrounding terrain has rendered, the player can move normally, and the game is still running version 20w17a.

steps.action: Locate the pre-existing filled Map in the inventory or hotbar. If necessary, press E, move that filled Map to a hotbar slot, close the inventory, and select its slot using the corresponding number key or mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E if needed; move the existing filled Map to the hotbar; E to close; select with hotbar key 1-9 or mouse wheel
steps.success_cue: The Map created in 20w16a is selected in the active hotbar slot and is visibly held by the player in the 20w17a world.

steps.action: While continuing to hold and view the pre-existing filled Map, walk or fly over the nearby surface that lies within the map's coverage. Use W for several seconds and keep the player marker within the map border so the map actively revisits and updates terrain from the upgraded world.
steps.exact_input: Hold W for several seconds; optionally use Space twice first if Creative flight is needed
steps.success_cue: The player has moved through previously mapped Overworld terrain in 20w17a while the existing filled Map remained selected and visible.

stor.handoff_condition: The pre-existing filled Map has just been carried across previously mapped surface terrain in the world after that world was upgraded from 20w16a to 20w17a. The Map is still selected and visible; begin observing its rendered contents now.
uncertainties: The issue contains no formal Steps to Reproduce section. The cross-version path is reconstructed from the description and comments stating that worlds from before 20w17a become affected when loaded in 20w17a.

The report does not designate one exact source version for creating the old world. This plan uses 20w16a as the immediately preceding snapshot and because the supplied issue context explicitly discusses upgrades from 20w16a to 20w17a.

The description most directly refers to looking at existing maps, while comments also state that newly created maps in an affected upgraded world can exhibit the issue. This plan uses an existing filled Map created before the upgrade because that most closely follows the original description.

No original world download, seed, coordinates, map identifier, map scale, or required amount of exploration is supplied. The plan therefore creates a small baseline map in an arbitrary 20w16a world and updates it in the same nearby area after upgrading.
Creative mode is not stated as a requirement. It is selected solely to obtain an Empty Map and traverse terrain deterministically without introducing crafting, resource collection, hunger, or combat.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 21w37a, unmodified vanilla client, single-player world using the integrated server, Creative mode, cheats enabled, and structure generation enabled. Use the report's explicitly labeled shipwreck route with seed -1899573754757393022.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected snapshot 21w37a rather than the fixed version 1.18 Pre-release 3.
Create a new world; do not reuse a world that has already generated or opened the target shipwreck chest.
Use seed -1899573754757393022 exactly, including the leading minus sign.
Enable Generate Structures so the shipwreck exists at the supplied location.
Use Creative mode and enable cheats so the supplied teleport command can be executed and the player cannot drown while positioned underwater.
Do not open or break any chest at the target shipwreck before the trigger step.
Use the shipwreck teleport route for this execution. The report also supplies other valid routes, but they are not needed for this deterministic plan.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation that uses snapshot 21w37a, launch it, and wait for the Minecraft main menu to appear.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left version text on the main menu identifies the running game as Minecraft Java Edition 21w37a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World. Set the game mode to Creative. Open More World Options and ensure Allow Cheats is ON and Generate Structures is ON.
steps.success_cue: The new-world screen shows Creative mode, cheats enabled, and structure generation enabled.

steps.action: In the Seed for the World Generator field, enter the report's shipwreck seed exactly. Do not omit the minus sign.
steps.success_cue: The seed field contains exactly -1899573754757393022.

steps.action: Select Create New World and wait until the player enters the world. Do not continue while the loading screen is visible; wait until terrain is rendered and normal player movement and camera movement respond.

uncertainties: The report characterizes the condition as intermittent, although the supplied seeds and coordinates are described as particularly good examples. A single clean attempt may therefore not activate the condition.

This plan selects the explicitly labeled shipwreck at /execute in minecraft:overworld run tp @s 2843.30 60.63 -977.73 255.15 36.00 because it avoids ambiguity about the structure type. source_meta._title: Map color for mangrove log is incorrect

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 22w11a in a new single-player Creative-mode Superflat world. Superflat is a practical choice that provides an unobstructed, level test area; the report does not require a particular seed, world type, or server.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 22w11a, not the fixed snapshot 22w12a or a later version.
Use a vanilla client without mods, datapacks, or resource packs that could alter blocks, maps, or rendering.
Create a new single-player world in Creative mode. Select the Superflat world type to provide a level outdoor test surface.
Use one newly initialized, unzoomed map for the entire reproduction. Do not replace it between block types.
Keep the acacia-log, stripped-mangrove-log, and mangrove-log test patches close together and within the area covered by that same map.
Place each log by using the top face of the ground so its axis is vertical and its cut end faces upward.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the launcher installation configured for snapshot 22w11a.
steps.exact_input: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation whose version is exactly "22w11a", then click Play.
steps.success_cue: The main-menu version text identifies the running game as Minecraft Java Edition 22w11a.

steps.action: Create a new single-player Creative-mode Superflat world.
steps.exact_input: Select Singleplayer -> Create New World; set Game Mode to Creative; open the additional world options, select the Superflat world type, and create the world.
steps.success_cue: The player enters a new world in Creative mode on a broad, level surface.

steps.action: Wait for the world to finish its initial loading before manipulating the map or blocks.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, player movement responds normally, and no world-loading screen remains visible.

steps.action: Choose a clear outdoor test area large enough for three adjacent 3-by-3 log patches with gaps between them.
steps.exact_input: Use the movement controls to stand near the center of a clear area at least 20 blocks long and 8 blocks wide.
steps.success_cue: The selected area is level, exposed to the sky, and free of blocks above the future log patches.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory.
steps.exact_input: Press E, or the rebound key for opening the inventory.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and its item tabs or search field are available.

steps.action: Obtain one Empty Map and place it in an unused hotbar slot.
steps.exact_input: Use the Creative inventory search field to search for "Empty Map", then click or drag one Empty Map into the hotbar at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: An Empty Map is visible in a hotbar slot.

steps.action: Obtain acacia logs and place a stack in an unused hotbar slot.
steps.exact_input: Search for "Acacia Log", then click or drag the Acacia Log item into the hotbar.
steps.success_cue: Acacia Log is visible in a hotbar slot and enough logs are available to place a 3-by-3 patch.

steps.action: Obtain stripped mangrove logs and place a stack in an unused hotbar slot.
steps.exact_input: Search for "Stripped Mangrove Log", then click or drag the Stripped Mangrove Log item into the hotbar.
steps.success_cue: Stripped Mangrove Log is visible in a hotbar slot and enough logs are available to place a 3-by-3 patch.

steps.action: Obtain unstripped mangrove logs and place a stack in an unused hotbar slot.
steps.exact_input: Search for "Mangrove Log" and select the item named exactly "Mangrove Log", not "Stripped Mangrove Log"; click or drag it into the hotbar.
steps.success_cue: Mangrove Log and Stripped Mangrove Log occupy separate hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the Creative inventory.
steps.exact_input: Press E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: Normal first-person world control resumes, and the Empty Map plus all three log types are visible in the hotbar.

steps.action: Select the Empty Map as the active hotbar item while standing near the center of the chosen test area.
steps.exact_input: Press the number key corresponding to the Empty Map's hotbar slot, or scroll the mouse wheel until the Empty Map is highlighted.
steps.success_cue: The Empty Map is shown in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Initialize the Empty Map at the test site.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once, or use the rebound Use Item/Place Block control once.
steps.success_cue: The Empty Map changes into an initialized map showing terrain around the player's current location.

steps.action: Keep the initialized map selected until the nearby test area has been drawn onto it.
steps.exact_input: Continue holding the map while standing or moving slowly around the selected test area; do not use a cartography table or otherwise zoom the map.
steps.success_cue: The map is no longer blank around the player marker, and the intended locations of all three nearby patches are inside its rendered area.

steps.action: Select the Acacia Log from the hotbar.
steps.exact_input: Press the corresponding hotbar number key or scroll until Acacia Log is the active item.
steps.success_cue: An Acacia Log is visible in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Place a 3-by-3 patch of upward-facing acacia logs on the level ground.
steps.exact_input: For each of nine adjacent ground positions arranged as a 3-by-3 square, aim at the top face of the ground block and right-click once. Do not place logs against the side of another log.
steps.success_cue: Nine acacia logs form a one-block-tall square, and every log has its cut end visible on top, confirming a vertical axis.

steps.action: Update the initialized map over the acacia-log patch without replacing or zooming the map.
steps.exact_input: Select the same initialized map from the hotbar and hold it while standing beside or walking around the acacia patch.
steps.success_cue: The footprint of the acacia patch is represented on the initialized map; no color judgment is made yet.

steps.action: Choose the location for the stripped-mangrove-log patch on the same level surface.
steps.exact_input: Move in a straight line from the acacia patch and leave at least three unchanged ground blocks between the edge of the acacia patch and the edge of the next 3-by-3 patch.
steps.success_cue: There is an empty, level 3-by-3 placement area separated from the acacia patch, and both locations remain within the initialized map's nearby coverage.

steps.action: Select the Stripped Mangrove Log from the hotbar.
steps.exact_input: Press the corresponding hotbar number key or scroll until Stripped Mangrove Log is the active item.
steps.success_cue: A Stripped Mangrove Log is visible in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Place a 3-by-3 patch of upward-facing stripped mangrove logs.
steps.exact_input: For each of the nine ground positions in the second 3-by-3 square, aim at the top face of the ground and right-click once.
steps.success_cue: Nine stripped mangrove logs form a one-block-tall square, every cut end faces upward, and the patch remains physically separate from the acacia patch.

steps.action: Update the same initialized map over the stripped-mangrove-log patch.
steps.exact_input: Select the initialized map and hold it while standing beside or walking around the stripped mangrove patch.
steps.success_cue: The footprints of both completed patches are represented on the same initialized map; no color judgment is made yet.

steps.action: Choose the location for the unstripped-mangrove-log patch, continuing the same row of patches.
steps.exact_input: Continue along the same straight line beyond the stripped mangrove patch, leaving at least three unchanged ground blocks before the third 3-by-3 placement area.
steps.success_cue: A third empty, level 3-by-3 area is available, separated from the first two patches and still close enough to remain on the same map.

steps.action: Select the unstripped Mangrove Log from the hotbar.
steps.exact_input: Press the corresponding hotbar number key or scroll until the item named "Mangrove Log" is active. Confirm that the selected item is not "Stripped Mangrove Log".
steps.success_cue: An unstripped Mangrove Log with bark on its sides is visible in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Place a 3-by-3 patch of upward-facing unstripped mangrove logs.
steps.exact_input: For each of the nine ground positions in the third 3-by-3 square, aim at the top face of the ground and right-click once.
steps.success_cue: Nine unstripped mangrove logs form a one-block-tall square, every cut end faces upward, and the three patches can be identified physically in order as acacia, stripped mangrove, then unstripped mangrove.

steps.action: Select the same initialized map and allow it to update over the unstripped-mangrove-log patch and the nearby comparison patches.
steps.exact_input: Select the initialized map, hold it in the active hand, and stand beside or move slowly around the third patch until all three patch footprints are present on the map.
steps.success_cue: The initialized map is actively held and contains the mapped locations of the three separate upward-facing log patches.

stor.handoff_condition: The same initialized, unzoomed map is being held immediately after it has updated over three nearby 3-by-3 patches arranged in known order: upward-facing acacia logs, upward-facing stripped mangrove logs, and upward-facing unstripped mangrove logs. Hand control to the observation subsystem for map-color comparison.
uncertainties: The report does not specify game mode, seed, world type, map scale, patch dimensions, or spacing. This plan uses a new Creative-mode Superflat world, a newly initialized unzoomed map, 3-by-3 patches, and gaps of at least three blocks as practical deterministic choices.

The phrase "obtain and fill a map" is interpreted as obtaining an Empty Map, initializing it, and allowing the local test area to render. The report does not clearly require exploration of every pixel in the map's full coverage area.

The report does not provide an exact physical arrangement for the log types. The straight-row order of acacia, stripped mangrove, and unstripped mangrove is chosen so the autonomous agent can distinguish the patches without adding labels or other blocks.
The attached images and video were not needed to execute the written reproduction and were not consulted.

source_meta._title: Map color for mangrove slab is incorrect

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 22w11a in a single-player Creative-mode world. Use an English (US) interface and default keyboard/mouse controls where possible. A new Superflat world is recommended to provide a clear, level test area without changing the map-color interaction under test.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher has snapshots enabled and can launch Java Edition snapshot 22w11a.
Do not use fix version 22w12a for this reproduction.
Use the unmodified 22w11a client without resource packs or datapacks that change the tested blocks or map rendering.
Have enough unobstructed, level ground to construct four 5-by-5 block patches within approximately 20 horizontal blocks of the point where the map is filled.
If controls have been rebound, use the bound equivalents of E for inventory, F3 for the debug display, right-click for use/place, and the hotbar selection keys or mouse wheel.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, start the installation whose version is exactly snapshot 22w11a. At the title screen, confirm that the displayed game version is 22w11a before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition title screen is open and identifies the running version as 22w11a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, cycle World Type to Superflat, return with Done, and create the world. No particular seed is required by the report.
steps.success_cue: A new Creative-mode Superflat world begins loading.

steps.action: Wait without beginning the test until the nearby flat terrain has rendered and normal movement responds immediately. Verify Creative mode by confirming that the player can fly after double-tapping Space and does not need to gather resources normally.
steps.success_cue: The surrounding Superflat terrain is fully visible, movement is responsive, and the player is in Creative mode.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, search separately for each listed item, and move the result into distinct hotbar slots: one Empty Map, one stack of Oak Planks, one stack of Oak Slabs, one stack of Mangrove Planks, and one stack of Mangrove Slabs. The hotbar is the nine-slot row displayed along the bottom of the screen. Close the inventory with E when finished.
steps.exact_input: Empty Map; Oak Planks; Oak Slab; Mangrove Planks; Mangrove Slab
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains an Empty Map and all four required construction items, including both mangrove items available in 22w11a.

steps.action: Move to the middle of a broad, unobstructed section of the flat world. Keep this location as the center of the test area so that every test patch can be built within about 20 horizontal blocks of it.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in an open, level area large enough for a roughly 13-by-13-block test layout.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Empty Map so that it is the active item in the player's main hand. With default controls, press the number key corresponding to its hotbar slot or scroll the mouse wheel until the map is selected.
steps.success_cue: The Empty Map is visibly held in the player's main hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Right-click once while holding the Empty Map to fill and initialize it at the test location. Do not right-click repeatedly.
steps.success_cue: The Empty Map has changed into a filled map and displays the surrounding terrain.

steps.action: Switch to any block item so that the filled map remains stored in the hotbar but is no longer held. Press F3 and orient the player so the debug display reports that the player is facing north. Reserve four 5-by-5 footprints in a two-by-two arrangement, with a three-block-wide gap between neighboring footprints: northwest for Oak Planks, northeast for Oak Slabs, southwest for Mangrove Planks, and southeast for Mangrove Slabs. Keep the entire arrangement within approximately 20 horizontal blocks of where the map was filled.
steps.success_cue: Four distinct 5-by-5 test footprints have been identified within the initialized map's nearby coverage, and their material assignments are known.

steps.action: Select Oak Planks and place a single horizontal layer of 25 blocks covering the entire northwest 5-by-5 footprint. Each position in the footprint should contain one oak plank block.
steps.success_cue: A complete 5-by-5 Oak Planks patch occupies the northwest position of the layout.

steps.action: Select Oak Slabs and cover the northeast 5-by-5 footprint with 25 individual slabs. Place each slab by right-clicking the top face of the ground once. Do not click a position twice, because two slabs in one position would form a double slab; break and replace any accidental double slab.
steps.success_cue: A complete 5-by-5 patch of single bottom Oak Slabs occupies the northeast position, with no double slabs.

steps.action: Select Mangrove Planks and place a single horizontal layer of 25 blocks covering the southwest 5-by-5 footprint. Each position in the footprint should contain one mangrove plank block.
steps.success_cue: A complete 5-by-5 Mangrove Planks patch occupies the southwest position of the layout.

steps.action: Select Mangrove Slabs and cover the southeast 5-by-5 footprint with 25 individual slabs. Place each slab by right-clicking the top face of the ground once. Do not place a second slab in the same position; break and replace any accidental double slab.
steps.success_cue: A complete 5-by-5 patch of single bottom Mangrove Slabs occupies the southeast position, with no double slabs.

steps.action: Confirm the physical layout before updating the map: Oak Planks northwest, Oak Slabs northeast, Mangrove Planks southwest, and Mangrove Slabs southeast. Confirm that the patches remain separated and that all four are near the location where the map was initialized.
steps.success_cue: All four labeled test patches are complete, distinct, and located inside the nearby mapped test area.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the filled map so it becomes the active item in the main hand. Slowly walk around or between the four patches while continuing to hold the map. Continue until all four patch footprints are represented on the map and the relevant portion of the map texture stops changing for at least two seconds. Keep the filled map selected when finished.
steps.success_cue: The filled map is active, all four test footprints have been updated onto it, and the map texture is no longer changing.

stor.handoff_condition: The filled map is selected in the active hotbar slot and has just finished refreshing after the Oak Planks, Oak Slabs, Mangrove Planks, and single Mangrove Slabs patches were placed. The physical two-by-two layout and its map representation are ready for the separate observation subsystem.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a seed, coordinates, world type, or game mode. A new Creative-mode Superflat world is selected as the simplest deterministic execution environment.

The report does not specify the size or arrangement of the block samples. Four separated 5-by-5 patches are used so each material occupies multiple visible map pixels and can be identified by position without relying on its displayed color.
The report does not specify whether the tested slabs are top or bottom slabs. This plan uses individual bottom slabs placed directly on the ground and explicitly avoids double slabs.
The report's phrase "obtain and fill a map" is interpreted as obtaining an Empty Map and right-clicking once to initialize it at the test site.
English item names and default controls are used for executable UI directions; equivalent localized labels or rebound controls may be used if necessary.
